_about: Why each class and relation exists, the alternatives considered, and who confirmed it. validated_by stays empty until a person who knows the domain confirms the entry.

Client.question: Which clients do we have?
Client.why: Everything the firm knows hangs from who it was for, so the client must exist once, with its own identity, however many engagements it has.
Client.alternatives: A client name written on each engagement: two spellings of one client would split its history, so it became a class.
Client.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Engagement.question: What work exists for each client, at what stage and in which service line?
Engagement.why: It is the unit every fact is traced to, and the context a person chooses before asking follow-up questions.
Engagement.alternatives: An opportunity and a project as two classes, as sales and delivery tools separate them. Rejected: the questions follow one piece of work across the signature, and splitting it would split its history.
Engagement.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Person.question: Who attended, said or decided something?
Person.why: Decisions and statements must be traced to the individual who made them, because a seat can change hands afterwards.
Person.alternatives: Roles alone: they are stable but cannot say who was actually in the room or who actually decided.
Person.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Role.question: Who sponsors, champions, pays or could block this, on either side?
Role.why: The same person can hold different seats on different engagements, and a seat can exist before anyone fills it, so the seat needs an identity of its own.
Role.alternatives: An attribute on the person: it cannot differ per engagement or be unfilled. Sales qualification practice supplies the role kinds, such as economic buyer and champion.
Role.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Interaction.question: Which meeting, presentation or call took place, and who attended?
Interaction.why: Who was present and what was shown are facts about the event, and 'what did we decide on the 14th' needs the event to have its own date.
Interaction.alternatives: Merging the meeting with its minutes: the two have different dates, and the event would have no home until someone wrote notes.
Interaction.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

DiscussionPoint.question: What was said, and who raised it?
DiscussionPoint.why: Asking what was said each time on a topic needs each statement separately, with its own speaker and meeting.
DiscussionPoint.alternatives: Free text in the meeting's summary: it cannot be grouped by topic or attributed to a speaker.
DiscussionPoint.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Topic.question: What keeps coming up with this client?
Topic.why: Seeing what recurs needs one identity shared by every mention of it.
Topic.alternatives: A tag on each discussion point: spelling drift would hide the recurrence that the question exists to find.
Topic.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

EngagementDocument.question: Which proposal, statement of work or deck exists, in which version, and is it internal or client-facing?
EngagementDocument.why: A version has its own status and audience, and an internal draft must stay distinguishable from what the client received.
EngagementDocument.alternatives: Reusing the core Document: that is a file in the corpus, and it has no version, status or audience. A separate class for the statement of work: nothing it holds differs from other documents, because scope and price have their own terms.
EngagementDocument.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

ScopeItem.question: What is in or out, and why did it change?
ScopeItem.why: Each line of scope can move on its own date for its own reason, so each needs its own history.
ScopeItem.alternatives: A scope paragraph on the statement of work: it could not say which line changed, when or why.
ScopeItem.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Deliverable.question: What do we owe, who accepts it, and has it been accepted?
Deliverable.why: Acceptance is tracked per item, with its own accepter and state.
Deliverable.alternatives: A list on the statement of work: it could not hold an accepter or an acceptance state per item.
Deliverable.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

SuccessCriterion.question: How will the work be judged?
SuccessCriterion.why: A criterion can be challenged and reworded before signature, and its history matters when acceptance is disputed.
SuccessCriterion.alternatives: A text attribute on the deliverable: criteria for the whole engagement would have no home, and a rewording would leave no trace.
SuccessCriterion.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Commitment.question: What did we promise, and does the statement of work cover it?
Commitment.why: A promise made in a deck or a meeting binds the relationship even when the contract is silent, and finding the gap needs the promise as a fact.
Commitment.alternatives: A kind of discussion point: a promise can sit in a document with no meeting behind it, and it needs links to the scope that covers or contradicts it.
Commitment.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Assumption.question: What do our plan and price rest on?
Assumption.why: Assumptions are what a change request is later argued from, so each must be findable and may name what it would trigger.
Assumption.alternatives: A paragraph in the statement of work: it cannot be checked one by one or linked to the change it triggers.
Assumption.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Milestone.question: What gates and checkpoints are coming, and what must clear first?
Milestone.why: Where an engagement stands is read from what has been met and what blocks the next one.
Milestone.alternatives: Project phases: no question needs them yet. A stage attribute alone: it cannot say what must clear.
Milestone.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Price.question: What are the fee, margin and contingency, and who approved them?
Price.why: A price is reworked and approved several times before signature, and each version needs its own date and approver.
Price.alternatives: Attributes on the engagement: superseding the engagement to record a new price would disturb everything linked to it.
Price.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Decision.question: What is waiting or decided, by whom, why, and against which options?
Decision.why: A decision has a date, a reason and rejected options, none of which a status can keep.
Decision.alternatives: A status on what it affects: it would keep no reason, no decider and no alternatives.
Decision.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Risk.question: What threatens this work, who owns it, and how has its rating changed?
Risk.why: Each risk is re-rated over time and has its own owner, so each needs its own history.
Risk.alternatives: A single risk list on the engagement: rating changes would leave no trace.
Risk.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Finding.question: What did we find, and on what evidence?
Finding.why: A finding must hold up when challenged, so it must trace to its evidence.
Finding.alternatives: Merging it with the recommendation: what is true and what to do about it are reviewed and disputed separately.
Finding.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Recommendation.question: What did we advise, and did the client act on it?
Recommendation.why: The firm follows up on advice, so each piece needs its own response.
Recommendation.alternatives: A section of the final deck: it could not record the client's response per item.
Recommendation.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

OpenItem.question: What is still open, who owns it, when is it due, and what does it block?
OpenItem.why: Follow-up is the reason this graph exists, and each item needs its own owner, due date and origin.
OpenItem.alternatives: Separate classes for actions, dependencies and issues, as project logs do: each holds the same facts here, so the difference is one attribute.
OpenItem.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

ChangeRequest.question: What triggered a change, what was the outcome, and what did it affect?
ChangeRequest.why: Change is how a fixed-fee engagement protects itself, and each request needs its trigger, outcome and effects.
ChangeRequest.alternatives: Only superseding the scope or the price: that shows what changed but not who asked, why or whether it was approved.
ChangeRequest.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

ReusableAsset.question: Which of the firm's methods can we reuse, and where have we used them?
ReusableAsset.why: Reuse across clients needs an identity that outlives any single engagement.
ReusableAsset.alternatives: A label on the engagement: it could not hold what the asset is or list everywhere it was used.
ReusableAsset.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

for_client.question: Which client is this work for?
for_client.why: This is half of the tracing rule: every engagement must name its client, so nothing floats free.
for_client.alternatives: A client on every fact: the same fact stated twice could disagree, so the client is reached through the engagement.
for_client.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

on_engagement.question: Which engagement does this belong to?
on_engagement.why: This is the other half of the tracing rule, and the engine refuses a fact of these kinds without it.
on_engagement.alternatives: Allowing several engagements: it would blur what belongs where. An item that truly spans two is recorded on each.
on_engagement.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

follows_on_from.question: What follow-on work did this engagement open up?
follows_on_from.why: Follow-on work is new work with its own scope and price, and the link keeps where it came from.
follows_on_from.alternatives: A list of possibilities on the first engagement: it could not track each one's stage.
follows_on_from.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

filled_by.question: Who holds this role?
filled_by.why: Separating the seat from the person lets the seat stay unfilled or change hands.
filled_by.alternatives: A name attribute on the role: it could not be linked to what the person said or decided.
filled_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

concerns_engagement.question: Which engagements did this meeting or document concern?
concerns_engagement.why: A meeting can cover several engagements, and a source document is often about one, so this is many-to-many and not required.
concerns_engagement.alternatives: Using the one-engagement link: it would refuse a meeting that covers two.
concerns_engagement.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

with_client.question: Which client was this interaction with?
with_client.why: General relationship meetings belong to no engagement, yet must still trace to a client.
with_client.alternatives: Inventing a catch-all engagement per client: it would pollute the list a person chooses from.
with_client.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

attended_by.question: Who attended?
attended_by.why: Knowing who has seen what is read from who attended and what was shown.
attended_by.alternatives: An attendee list as text: it could not answer what one person has seen.
attended_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

presented.question: What was presented, and to whom?
presented.why: Avoiding surprises at a readout depends on knowing what each person has already seen.
presented.alternatives: Recording readers on the document: it would lose when and in which meeting they saw it.
presented.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

recorded_in.question: Where is this meeting written down?
recorded_in.why: Keeps the event and its record separate while still linked.
recorded_in.alternatives: Merging them, already rejected for the interaction itself.
recorded_in.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

said_in.question: Where was this said?
said_in.why: Ties every statement to its meeting, and through it to the client.
said_in.alternatives: Tying statements directly to an engagement: statements in a general client meeting would have no home.
said_in.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

raised_by.question: Who raised it?
raised_by.why: The question asks who raised each topic, and a statement must be attributable.
raised_by.alternatives: Keeping the speaker in the text: it could not be queried.
raised_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

about_topic.question: What was this about?
about_topic.why: It is what lets mentions across meetings be grouped.
about_topic.alternatives: A free-text tag, already rejected for topic.
about_topic.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

raised_in.question: Which meeting did this come from?
raised_in.why: Follow-up needs to go back to where the item was agreed, and it is how a meeting's outcomes are listed.
raised_in.alternatives: Text in the summary: it could not list what a meeting left open.
raised_in.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

defined_in.question: Which document says this?
defined_in.why: Comparing what a version promised with what is true now needs the link.
defined_in.alternatives: Relying only on the citation: that names the file, not the business document and its version.
defined_in.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

accepted_by.question: Who accepts it?
accepted_by.why: An acceptance dispute starts with not knowing who could accept.
accepted_by.alternatives: A person only: often only the seat is known when the work is signed.
accepted_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

judges.question: By what test is this accepted?
judges.why: Links a test to what it tests, so an acceptance dispute can start from an agreed test.
judges.alternatives: A text field on the deliverable, already rejected for success criterion.
judges.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

made_in.question: Where was this promised?
made_in.why: A disputed promise is settled by where it was made.
made_in.alternatives: Citation alone: it names a file, not the meeting.
made_in.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

made_by.question: Who promised it?
made_by.why: The promise has to be raised with whoever made it.
made_by.alternatives: Leaving it in the text: it could not be queried.
made_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

covered_by.question: Does the statement of work cover this promise?
covered_by.why: A promise with no cover is exactly what the question is looking for.
covered_by.alternatives: A yes-or-no attribute: it would not say what covers it.
covered_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

contradicted_by.question: Does the statement of work contradict this promise?
contradicted_by.why: A promise the contract excludes is more urgent than one it merely omits.
contradicted_by.alternatives: Treating both as uncovered: it hides the urgent case.
contradicted_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

approved_by.question: Who approved the price?
approved_by.why: A price gap needs a named approver, or it returns later as a margin problem.
approved_by.alternatives: Free text: it could not be queried.
approved_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

decided_by.question: Who must decide, or who decided?
decided_by.why: A waiting decision without a decider stays waiting.
decided_by.alternatives: Two relations for before and after: the state attribute already says which.
decided_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

taken_in.question: Where was it decided?
taken_in.why: Makes 'what did we decide at that meeting' answerable.
taken_in.alternatives: The date alone: two meetings can share a date.
taken_in.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

blocks.question: What is blocked until then?
blocks.why: This is how a gate's conditions and a decision's consequences are read.
blocks.alternatives: A blocked flag on the item: it would not say by what.
blocks.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

owned_by.question: Who owns it?
owned_by.why: Follow-up needs an owner, and documents often name only the seat.
owned_by.alternatives: A person only: it would refuse a seat with no name yet.
owned_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

became.question: Did this risk happen?
became.why: Project practice moves a risk that occurs into the issues, and the link keeps the trail.
became.alternatives: Closing the risk and starting afresh: the history would be lost.
became.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

evidenced_by.question: What evidence supports it?
evidenced_by.why: A finding must hold up when a steering committee challenges it, so its evidence must be reachable.
evidenced_by.alternatives: Citation alone: an interaction with no written record could not count as evidence.
evidenced_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

addresses.question: Which finding led to this advice?
addresses.why: Links what to do to why, so advice can be reviewed against the finding it came from.
addresses.alternatives: Merging them, already rejected for finding.
addresses.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

changes.question: What did the change affect?
changes.why: The effect on scope, fee and dates is what the question asks.
changes.alternatives: Text in the request: it could not be traced from the scope item.
changes.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)

uses_asset.question: Where has this method been used?
uses_asset.why: Reuse is read from where an asset has been used.
uses_asset.alternatives: A label on the engagement, already rejected for reusable asset.
uses_asset.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-03 (walked through in the ontology interview)
